errors.text: The proposed Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo cast/SPD route does not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiTi powder-metallurgy route based on high-energy ball milling and spark-plasma sintering.
The nominal starting alloy contains 5 at.% Mo, while the hypothesis states that Mo must remain below approximately 4 at.% to avoid instability.
The cited microalloying evidence reports that 0.5 at.% carbon suppresses the FCC/HCP constitution and produces single-phase FCC, contrary to using carbon in the proposed dual-phase FCC/HCP material.

No cited evidence establishes that annealing this Mo-containing alloy at 600-700 degrees C for 1-2 hours preserves sub-50 nm grains and avoids precipitates; the thermal-stability evidence instead warns of phase decomposition during medium-temperature or prolonged annealing.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary or phase-boundary strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because it lacks composition-matched controls with systematically varied grain size or phase fraction.
